story.headline: Australian wages rose 1.1% in the September quarter, the strongest quarterly growth since December 2023, but at 3.5% over the year still trail 4.3% inflation, two weeks after the RBA lifted rates to 4.85%
story.why: Australian relevance 3/3 (every worker and borrower; feeds the RBA's December call); debate 2/2 (rate-hike risk vs overdue catch-up after four quarters of falling real wages); measurable 2/2 (ABS WPI 1.1% q/q, 3.5% y/y; CPI 4.3%; cash rate 4.85%); timeliness 2/3 (published by the ABS at 11:30am AEDT Wed 18 Nov, about 19 hours before this 6:48am AEDT run; no fresher story scored higher). linkedin.post:
1.1%: how much Australian wages rose in the September quarter, the strongest since December 2023, the ABS said yesterday.

Over the year wages grew 3.5%, still behind 4.3% inflation. The RBA lifted rates to 4.85% this month; Governor Michele Bullock said board members who voted to hold saw "no sign of wages growth accelerating". EY's Cherelle Murphy calls the pace "uncomfortably high" but expects a December hold. Treasurer Jim Chalmers blames inflation, not pay, for falling real wages.

If wages still trail prices, is their fastest rise since 2023 a rate-rise risk or overdue catch-up? Tell us what you think below.

#AusSight #ausbiz
